seoTitle: How to Track an eBay Order for Any Carrier (2026)
metaDescription: Find your eBay order's tracking number, read the carrier's status timeline right inside eBay, and get help if a package hasn't arrived.
intro: Once an item ships, knowing exactly where your package is takes the guesswork out of waiting for delivery, and eBay actually pulls the carrier's scan history directly into your order page rather than leaving you to copy a tracking number elsewhere. This guide follows the real purchase history and shipment details screens, showing what a tracked order looks like from the order list down to the individual delivery scans, plus where to go if a package seems stuck.

steps.heading: Open Purchase History and find the order
steps.body: From My eBay, go to Purchase History to see every order you've placed, each listed with its order date, item, seller, and total. A shipped and delivered order shows a green confirmation banner right in the list — "Delivered on [date]" — along with the tracking number itself, so in many cases you don't even need to click into the order to know it arrived.

image.caption: An order in Purchase History showing a green "Delivered on Sat, May 20" confirmation with its tracking number listed directly in the order row.

steps.heading: Open the shipment details for the full scan history
steps.body: Click the tracking number and a Shipment details window opens showing the carrier (USPS, FedEx, UPS, or another service), the tracking number again for reference, and a visual progress bar moving through Accepted, In Transit, and Delivered. Below that sits the full scan-by-scan history — sorting and processing complete, arrival at unit, out for delivery, delivered in/at mailbox — each with its own timestamp and location. This is the real-time detail eBay's own order list doesn't show, and it's the fastest way to see exactly where a package is right now.

image.caption: The Shipment details popup, showing carrier, tracking number, a status bar, and a timestamped scan history down to the delivery location.

steps.heading: Check the carrier's own site for more detail
steps.body: eBay's shipment details window notes that "tracking information may be transmitted with a delay," so if you need the absolute latest scan, paste the same tracking number into the carrier's own website — USPS, FedEx, or UPS — for real-time updates. This matters most in the final stretch of delivery, when minutes can matter and eBay's cached view might be a scan or two behind the carrier's live system.

steps.heading: Understand what each status means
steps.body: The three-stage bar — Accepted, In Transit, Delivered — is a simplified view of a much longer scan history underneath it. "Accepted" means the carrier has the package but hasn't started moving it yet; "In Transit" can last anywhere from hours to several days depending on distance and service level; "Out for delivery" means it's on a truck that day. A status that hasn't changed in several days despite showing "In Transit" is the point to start paying closer attention, though a day or two of no movement is often normal, especially over a weekend.

steps.heading: Track eBay's Global Shipping Program the same way
steps.body: If your order routed through eBay's Global Shipping Program because you bought from an international seller, it still generates its own tracking number and shows up in Purchase History the same way — the shipment details popup works identically, though GSP packages often show two tracking legs: one to the GSP facility and a second for the final domestic leg to you.

steps.heading: Get help if tracking stalls
steps.body: If a shipment shows no movement well past its estimated delivery date, start by messaging the seller directly through the order page — most delays get resolved at this stage. If that doesn't get a response, eBay's Customer Service section offers direct help articles for exactly this situation, including "Get help with an item that hasn't arrived" and "Tracking your item," both listed as quick, popular articles rather than buried in a generic help search.

image.caption: eBay's Customer Service page, with "Tracking your item" and "Get help with an item that hasn't arrived" listed as popular suggested articles.

steps.heading: Escalate through eBay if the seller doesn't respond
steps.body: When a seller doesn't reply within a reasonable window, or tracking shows "delivered" but nothing actually arrived, eBay's buyer protection and resolution tools step in from the same Customer Service area. Check with neighbors or a building's mail room first for a delivered-but-missing package, since that resolves a surprising number of cases before you need to open a formal case at all.

faq.question: What if my eBay order has no tracking number yet?
faq.answer: Some sellers add tracking a day or two after the sale. Check back on the order in Purchase History, and message the seller if it's been longer than their stated handling time.

faq.question: Why does my tracking status say 'in transit' for days?
faq.answer: This is common with standard carrier services and doesn't necessarily mean a problem, but if it persists well past the estimated delivery date, check the carrier's own site or contact the seller.

faq.question: Can I track eBay's Global Shipping Program packages the same way?
faq.answer: Yes, GSP shipments generate their own tracking number that appears in Purchase History and opens the same Shipment details view, though they often show two separate tracking legs.

faq.question: What should I do if tracking shows delivered but I never received it?
faq.answer: Check with neighbors or your building's mail room first, then contact the seller, and if it's still unresolved, use eBay's Customer Service help articles to open a case through buyer protection.
